::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
This page is not part of the main dhbern.github.io navigation. It is a companion resource for the lecture series **Digital Humanities — Introductions** (FS 2027). Lecturer bios are AI-generated from public academic profiles, checked against them and marked accordingly; Cerstin Mahlow's bio is her own.
:::

## About the Series

The *Digital Humanities — Introductions* lecture series brings together 17 researchers from Swiss and European universities to present major research areas and methods in Digital Humanities. Lectures are fully online, can be worked through in any order, and are assessed via an open-book multiple-choice exam.

**Exam:** date tba (end of the spring semester 2027) · 60 minutes · 20 randomly selected questions · 4 options each · no negative marking  
**Consultation:** two sessions, dates tba (spring semester 2027) · via Zoom/ILIAS

```{=html}
  ];
  // Every link cites the lecture summary on its page (Overview, Main Points, Examples Mentioned).
  const topics = [
    { id: 'recognition', label: 'Text & music recognition', links: [
      [1, 'Workflow from layout analysis to line-level recognition and keyword search'],
      [11, 'NLP can assist with OCR post-processing and normalization'],

    { id: 'corpora', label: 'Corpora', links: [

      [8, 'Corpora as large, machine-readable collections of texts'],
      [11, 'Parallel corpora for training translation systems'],

      [14, 'Medieval and early modern corpora'] ] },
    { id: 'language', label: 'Language as data', links: [

      [8, 'Language studied through observation of real usage'],
      [11, 'Making text collections accessible and analyzable'] ] },
    { id: 'annotation', label: 'Annotation & named entities', links: [
      [8, 'Metadata and linguistic annotation in corpora'],
      [11, 'Named entity recognition among large-scale text tasks'],
      [14, 'Recognized text as basis for named entity recognition and linking'] ] },
    { id: 'editions', label: 'Encoding & digital editions', links: [
      [4, 'TEI as the de facto standard for digital scholarly editing'],
      [13, 'Music encoding (MEI) and digital editions'] ] },
    { id: 'graphs', label: 'Graphs, networks & linked data', links: [
      [4, 'Graph-based models as alternatives to hierarchical markup'],
      [6, 'Graph databases, RDF triples and linked open data'],
      [10, 'Entities and relations represented as nodes and edges'] ] },
    { id: 'metadata', label: 'Metadata & classification', links: [
      [5, 'Library catalogs, indexes and structured book data'],
      [6, 'Metadata gives digital objects context and meaning'],
      [9, 'What bits mean depends on format, metadata and interpretation'],
      [12, 'Socially produced categories can appear neutral'],
      [15, 'Provenance, original order and hierarchical archival description'] ] },
    { id: 'modelling', label: 'Modelling as interpretation', links: [
      [3, 'Digital linguistics defined through formal modeling'],
      [4, 'Editions represent texts and create a theory of the corpus'],
      [7, 'A model-centered definition of digital humanities'],
      [10, 'Every network model is an interpretive abstraction'],
      [14, 'Critical about what counts as text and what is being modeled'] ] },
    { id: 'critique', label: 'Methodological critique', links: [
      [5, 'Sampling and the gap between available data and the full population'],
      [7, 'Critiques of uncritical tool adoption'],
      [12, 'Against data idealism'],
      [14, 'Biases and limitations of the pipeline'] ] },
    { id: 'power', label: 'Gender, power & data feminism', links: [
      [2, 'Gender and technology are co-constructed; Data Feminism'],
      [8, 'Political language and gendered language use'],
      [12, 'Feminist methods, data feminism and platform power'] ] },

      [4, 'The Gospel of John in multiple manuscript witnesses'],
      [10, 'Reformation correspondence networks'],
      [13, 'Historical and non-European notation systems'],
      [14, 'Medieval and early modern documents'] ] }
  ];

  const COLOR = { text: '#6366f1', data: '#06b6d4', critical: '#ec4899', case: '#f59e0b' };
  const GROUPS = [['text', 'Text & Language'], ['data', 'Data & Infrastructure'], ['critical', 'Critical Perspectives'], ['case', 'Case Studies']];
  const root = document.getElementById('topic-network');
  const tip = root.querySelector('.tn-tip');
  const links = topics.flatMap(t => t.links.map(([lid, ev]) => ({ topic: t, lecture: lectures[lid - 1], ev })));

  function draw() {
    root.querySelectorAll('svg').forEach(s => s.remove());
    const W = root.clientWidth;
    const narrow = W < 620;
    root.classList.toggle('tn-narrow', narrow);
    if (narrow) return; // small screens get the table below instead
    const ROW = 30, GAP = 26, TOP = 30;
    const xL = Math.min(250, W * 0.32), xR = W - Math.min(250, W * 0.30);

    // left column: lectures grouped by theme
    let y = TOP;
    const heads = [];
    GROUPS.forEach(([key, label]) => {
      heads.push({ key, label, y });
      y += GAP - 4;
      lectures.filter(l => l.theme === key).forEach(l => { l.y = y; y += ROW; });
      y += 6;
    });
    const H = y + 10;
    // right column: topics ordered by the mean position of their lectures, to keep lines short
    topics.forEach(t => { t.bary = d3.mean(t.links, ([id]) => lectures[id - 1].y); });
    const order = topics.slice().sort((a, b) => a.bary - b.bary);
    const step = (H - TOP - 20) / (order.length - 1);
    order.forEach((t, i) => { t.y = TOP + 10 + i * step; });

    const svg = d3.select(root).insert('svg', '.tn-tip')
      .attr('viewBox', [0, 0, W, H]).attr('width', W).attr('height', H)
      .attr('role', 'img')
      .attr('aria-label', 'Diagram linking the 17 lectures to ' + topics.length + ' shared topics. A table version follows below.');

    svg.append('g').selectAll('text').data(heads).join('text')
      .attr('x', xL + 8).attr('y', d => d.y + 6).attr('text-anchor', 'end')
      .attr('font-size', 11).attr('font-weight', 700).attr('letter-spacing', '.06em')
      .attr('fill', d => COLOR[d.key]).text(d => d.label.toUpperCase());

    const path = d => {
      const x1 = xL + 8, y1 = d.lecture.y, x2 = xR - 8, y2 = d.topic.y, m = (x1 + x2) / 2;
      return `M${x1},${y1} C${m},${y1} ${m},${y2} ${x2},${y2}`;
    };
    const link = svg.append('g').attr('fill', 'none').selectAll('path').data(links).join('path')
      .attr('d', path).attr('stroke', d => COLOR[d.lecture.theme]).attr('stroke-opacity', 0.5).attr('stroke-width', 1.8);
    const hit = svg.append('g').attr('fill', 'none').selectAll('path').data(links).join('path')
      .attr('d', path).attr('stroke', 'transparent').attr('stroke-width', 10).style('cursor', 'help');

    const lec = svg.append('g').selectAll('a').data(lectures).join('a')
      .attr('href', d => d.file.replace('.qmd', '.html')).attr('class', 'tn-node-lecture')
      .attr('aria-label', d => `Lecture ${d.id}: ${d.short} (${d.name})`)
      .attr('transform', d => `translate(${xL},${d.y})`);
    lec.append('circle').attr('cx', 8).attr('r', 6).attr('fill', d => COLOR[d.theme]);
    lec.append('text').attr('x', -4).attr('dy', '0.35em').attr('text-anchor', 'end')
      .attr('font-size', 13).attr('fill', '#0f172a')
      .text(d => `${d.id} · ${d.short}`);

    const top = svg.append('g').selectAll('g').data(topics).join('g')
      .attr('transform', d => `translate(${xR},${d.y})`).style('cursor', 'default');
    top.append('rect').attr('x', -8).attr('y', -6).attr('width', 12).attr('height', 12).attr('rx', 3)
      .attr('fill', '#f1f5f9').attr('stroke', '#64748b');
    top.append('text').attr('x', 12).attr('dy', '0.35em').attr('font-size', 13).attr('font-weight', 600)
      .attr('fill', '#0f172a').text(d => d.label);

    function place(evt) {
      const r = root.getBoundingClientRect();
      let x = evt.clientX - r.left + 14, yy = evt.clientY - r.top + 14;
      if (x + tip.offsetWidth > r.width - 8) x = evt.clientX - r.left - tip.offsetWidth - 14;
      tip.style.left = Math.max(8, x) + 'px'; tip.style.top = yy + 'px';
    }
    function show(html, evt) { tip.innerHTML = html; tip.style.opacity = 1; place(evt); }
    function focus(keep) {
      link.classed('tn-dim', d => !keep(d));
      lec.classed('tn-dim', l => !links.some(d => keep(d) && d.lecture === l));
      top.classed('tn-dim', t => !links.some(d => keep(d) && d.topic === t));
    }
    function reset() { tip.style.opacity = 0; link.classed('tn-dim', false); lec.classed('tn-dim', false); top.classed('tn-dim', false); }

    lec.on('mouseenter focus', (evt, l) => {
      focus(d => d.lecture === l);
      show(`<b>${l.id} · ${l.short}</b><br>${l.name}<br><em>${links.filter(d => d.lecture === l).map(d => d.topic.label).join(' · ')}</em>`, evt);
    }).on('mousemove', place).on('mouseleave blur', reset);
    top.on('mouseenter', (evt, t) => {
      focus(d => d.topic === t);
      show(`<b>${t.label}</b><br>Lectures ${t.links.map(([id]) => id).sort((a, b) => a - b).join(', ')}`, evt);
    }).on('mousemove', place).on('mouseleave', reset);
    hit.on('mouseenter click', (evt, d) => {
      focus(x => x === d);
      show(`<b>${d.lecture.id} · ${d.lecture.short}</b> → ${d.topic.label}<br><em>${d.ev}</em>`, evt);
    }).on('mousemove', place).on('mouseleave', reset);
  }
  draw();
  let rt; window.addEventListener('resize', () => { clearTimeout(rt); rt = setTimeout(draw, 150); });

  // Text version of the same data, for screen readers and small screens
  const det = document.createElement('details');
  det.innerHTML = '<summary>Topics and lectures as a table</summary>' +
    // tag names split so Quarto does not try to parse this string as a raw HTML table
    '<' + 'table class="table tn-table"><thead><tr><th>Topic</th><th>Lectures</th></tr></thead><tbody>' +
    topics.map(t => `<tr><td>${t.label}</td><td>${t.links.map(([id, ev]) => { const l = lectures[id - 1]; return `<a href="${l.file.replace('.qmd', '.html')}">${id} ${l.short}</a>: ${ev}`; }).join('<br>')}</td></tr>`).join('') +
    '</tbody></' + 'table>';
  root.nextElementSibling.after(det);
})();
</script>
```

The 17 lectures span four interconnected themes drawn from the introductory podcast:

- **Text** — digitization, recognition, editing, and linguistic analysis of texts (Lectures 1, 3, 4, 8, 11, 14)
- **Data & Infrastructure** — imaging, linked data, network analysis, archives (Lectures 9, 6, 10, 15)
- **Critical Perspectives** — theory, gender, materiality, photography (Lectures 2, 7, 12, 16)
- **Case Studies** — book history, musicology, game studies (Lectures 5, 13, 17)

```{=html}
    { num:17, name:'Yannick Rochat',     inst:'University of Lausanne',   topic:'Game Studies',            lat:46.522,  lng:6.572,  theme:'case'     }
  ];

  const themeLabel = { text:'Text & Language', data:'Data & Infrastructure', critical:'Critical Perspectives', case:'Case Studies' };

  // Jitter overlapping markers slightly
  const seen = {};
  lecturers.forEach(l => {
    const key = `${l.lat.toFixed(2)},${l.lng.toFixed(2)}`;
    seen[key] = (seen[key] || 0) + 1;
    if (seen[key] > 1) { l.lat += (Math.random()-0.5)*0.02; l.lng += (Math.random()-0.5)*0.02; }
  });

  lecturers.forEach(l => {
    const color = THEME[l.theme];
    const icon = L.divIcon({
      className: '',
      html: `<div style="width:30px;height:30px;border-radius:50%;background:${color};
               border:3px solid white;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);
               display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;
               font-size:11px;font-weight:800;color:white;cursor:pointer">${l.num}</div>`,
      iconSize: [30, 30], iconAnchor: [15, 15]
    });
    L.marker([l.lat, l.lng], { icon })
      .addTo(map)
      .bindPopup(`<strong>${l.num}. ${l.name}</strong><br>${l.inst}<br><em>${l.topic}</em><br>
        <span style="font-size:11px;color:#6366f1">${themeLabel[l.theme]}</span>`);
  });

  // Legend
  const legend = L.control({ position: 'bottomright' });
  legend.onAdd = () => {
    const d = L.DomUtil.create('div');
    d.style.cssText = 'background:white;padding:10px 12px;border-radius:8px;font-size:12px;line-height:1.8;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.2)';
    d.innerHTML = Object.entries(themeLabel).map(([k,v]) =>
      `<span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:${THEME[k]};margin-right:6px;vertical-align:middle"></span>${v}`
    ).join('<br>');
    return d;
  };
  legend.addTo(map);
})();
</script>
```
